proposal.hypothesis: The catalog has seven distinct valid programs; unaligned SIMD measured 0.079892 s, runtime-peeled 16-byte SIMD measured 0.079254 s, and the 32-byte alignment variant measured 0.080007 s, while 64-byte alignment was slower at 0.087704 s. This candidate tests a different factor: guarded OpenMP SIMD with simdlen(4), without an alignment claim or peel, to see whether limiting concurrent x iterations improves the frozen compiler's lowering. These prior measurements do not predict this candidate's outcome.

retained: Keep the unfused single-timestep stencil, arithmetic order, and existing interior bounds unchanged.
Guard an OpenMP simdlen(4) directive on the contiguous x-loop with the OpenMP 4.0 version check; compile the same scalar loop otherwise.
Make no alignment claim or scalar-peeling assumption, preserving correctness when the interior begins at a non-aligned offset.
Do not alter compiler flags, threading, spatial blocking, or temporal blocking.
